title: Connect AI clients
subtitle: Point coding agents, desktop AI agents, IDE extensions, or any OpenAI-compatible LLM client at celer-route. Pick a client and model set — we generate the ready-to-paste config.

stepHint.client: Confirm which client to wire in — the rest of the wizard adapts to it.
stepHint.endpoint: The base URL and API key become fixed inputs in every generated config; switching clients later won't lose them.
stepHint.endpointProtocol: opencode only: the generated config talks to the Responses API when checked, Chat Completions otherwise.
stepHint.modelsSubset: {{agent}} writes these models into the config. The list comes from the API key you selected.
stepHint.modelsDefault: If no default model is picked, the client will prompt for one on startup.
stepHint.output: Paste each tab into the matching place in your client. You can always jump back to revise earlier steps.
stepHint.apiKey: The model list and default model update with the visible scope of the API key you select.

platformHint: The generated config paths, environment-variable syntax, and setup steps adapt to the OS you pick.

agent.openaiCompatible: Other OpenAI-compatible client (hermes / openclaw / aider / goose / …)

responsesProtocol: Use Responses API (@ai-sdk/openai) instead of Chat API
baseUrlHint: Origin of your celer-route instance. The correct surface (/v1 or /anthropic) is appended automatically per client.
apiKeyEmpty: No API keys yet. Create one under Governance → API Keys.
apiKeyOptional: Inference auth is disabled — the generated config omits the API key.
defaultModelHint: Defaults to every model this API key can see (fetched from /v1/models).
applyTabDescription: Paste and run this in your terminal — it backs up the existing config (if any), merges the new values, and prints the path it wrote to. Only matching keys are overwritten; everything else is preserved.
applyTabShellHint: The command is wrapped in sh -c, so bash, zsh, fish, or any other POSIX terminal runs it as-is — no shell switching needed.
fileTabDescription: Final contents of {{path}}. Identical to what the apply command writes. Use this when you want to drop it into a script, dotfiles repo, or paste manually.
envTabDescription: `export` these before launching the client and the client talks to celer-route with no config file changes. Handy for quick tests, CI, and remote dev boxes.
testTabDescription: Paste into a terminal. A 200 response confirms the base URL, API key, and default model are wired through correctly; any 4xx/5xx surfaces verbatim so you can debug.
noOutput: Select at least one model to generate a config.
